subject: Reserved capacity sizing & SKU mix — approval for discount
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@datascale.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing for reserved capacity / tentative Q4 ramp
Attachments: initial_usage_snapshot.csv (csv)

Hey Rafael,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. We want to get ahead of capacity for a paid pilot with DataScale — target start date Oct 1. High level: we expect ~2M tokens/day steady-state by month 2, peaky traffic during business hours (2.5x), and our models are a mix of chat-like agents (similar to GPT-style chat) plus embedding-heavy search reranks.

Two quick asks: can you propose a SKU mix (A100 vs H100 / vRAM, or equivalent) + a 12 vs 24 month reserved commit comparison (cost + expected headroom) so procurement can budget? Also procurement will want a proforma invoice and SOC2 evidence.

If helpful, attaching a small snapshot of our current usage.

— Alex
Head of ML Platforms
DataScale
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@datascale.ai>
Cc: karn@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing for reserved capacity / tentative Q4 ramp
Attachments: reserved_capacity_model_v3.csv (csv)

Alex —

Appreciate the details — included a first-pass sizing model attached (SKU mix + latency SLO assumptions). Quick summary of recommendations:

- SKU mix: 60% H100-large-equivalent for chat (low latency, KV cache heavy), 40% A100/8x for batch embedding and rerank workloads.
- Baseline commit: 12-month reserve covers expected steady-state with 20% headroom; 24-month gives ~12% additional discount but increases risk if usage changes.
- Pricing sensitivity: moving from 12->24 months starts to unlock discounts in the 10–18% band depending on guaranteed throughput; >20% requires exec approval.

Questions for procurement: do you require explicit per-token billing guarantees or is a monthly committed vGPU-hour okay? Also confirm latency SLO (p95) and any region constraints.

I flagged the model with suggested provisioning and a conservative burst buffer. Sharing to procurement/finance will speed things up — if you want, I can prepare a proforma based on the 12-month with an optional 24-month uplift.

— Rafael
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Green <alex.green@datascale.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing for reserved capacity / tentative Q4 ramp

Rafael — thanks. Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for chat. Model profile: mostly Llama2-70B style for agents, embeddings model is smaller but high concurrency. Region: us-west preferred.

Procurement note: they're looking for a pricing threshold — leadership wants to see if a 24-month commitment gets to >=20% effective discount vs on-demand unit economics. If not, they'll push for 12-month. Also they asked for SOC2 and a proforma they can attach to the PO.

Can you put together two line-item proformas (12m / 24m) and call out the SKU mix + how billing will appear (committed vGPU-hours + overage). Procurement@datascale will loop in legal for T&Cs.

— Alex
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: DataScale proforma & discount request (need approval path)
Attachments: proforma_invoice_v2.xlsx (xlsx); reserved_capacity_model_v3.csv (csv)

Team —

Fwd'ing a customer request (DataScale). They want two proformas (12m vs 24m) and leadership is specifically asking whether a 24-month gets them >=20% off effective unit price. My model shows ~12–15% for a conservative 24m commit for the SKU mix below; to reach 20% we'd need to either: (a) increase guaranteed throughput (higher commit), (b) extend to 36 months, or (c) approve an additional strategic discount.

Key ask: do we have latitude to approve up to 22% discount for strategic deals in this region (US west, potential ARR $1.2M/year on committed spend)? If no, what's the maximum we can offer without C-level approval? Also need finance to confirm invoicing cadence and if we can issue a proforma with net-30 PO terms.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa: approve maximum commercial discount band we can offer without escalation.
- Karthik: confirm if any product-side constraints on SKU mix that would force a different pricing tier.
- Dylan (finance): quick sanity-check on net-30 proforma and whether we need prepayment for >15% discounts.

Appreciate quick turnaround — procurement is on a short timeline.

— Rafael
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T14:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: DataScale proforma & discount request (need approval path)

Rafael —

We can approve up to an 18% effective discount for a 12-month committed deal without running to the executive committee, provided finance signs off on net-30. Anything above 18% requires VP approval and a documented strategic rationale (potential logo value or expansion motion).

Karthik — if there's no technical constraint with the proposed 60/40 H100/A100 split, we should proceed with the 12m @ 18% and include an optional 24m pricing line that shows the marginal uplift if they want to extend.

Dylan — please confirm whether finance needs prepayment language for discounts >15% or if net-30 is acceptable here.

— Marissa
VP, Commercials
Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@datascale.ai>, Procurement <procurement@datascale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity proforma & next steps (12m commit, approved)
Attachments: proforma_invoice_v2.xlsx (xlsx); datascale_soc2_packet.pdf (pdf)

Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the revised proforma: 12-month reserved capacity, SKU mix 60% H100-equivalent + 40% A100-equivalent, with an 18% effective discount (approved by our commercial lead). Billing will appear as a monthly committed vGPU-hour line item with overage billed at on-demand rates; proforma shows sample month-by-month charges.

We also attached a SOC2 packet for your legal team. Next steps:
- Procurement: confirm PO terms (net-30) and send PO to ar@redwood.com.
- Legal: we can accept standard DataScale T&Cs subject to minor commercial redlines.
- Execution: once PO received, we provision reserved pool (typically 7–10 business days for dedicated fleet provisioning in us-west) and schedule an onboarding runbook.

DocuSign link for the commercial addendum: https://docusign.com/rooms/abcdef (placeholder)

If you want a 24-month alternative pricing line, I can provide it as an appendix but leadership has requested we default to the 12m @ 18% unless there's a clear exec ask.

— Rafael
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
